knowledgePattern: Compare prime exponents in a product-of-powers identity

hints.title: Use prime bases
hints.body: Rewrite each numerical base as powers of its prime factors, then gather all contributions to each prime exponent.
hints.recap: Multiplying powers of the same base adds their exponents.
hints.pitfall: An outer exponent multiplies every exponent in the factorised base.
hints.pause: Write the total exponent of each prime on each side.

recall.reminder: Multiplying powers of the same base adds their exponents.

hints.title: Compare each prime separately
hints.body: Equal positive rational numbers have equal net exponents of each prime in their prime factorisations. Use these equations together.
hints.recap: Unique prime factorisation lets the exponent of each prime be compared separately.
hints.pitfall: Keep the constant exponent contributions as well as those involving variables.
hints.pause: Simplify the relations and calculate the requested sum, checking positivity.

recall.reminder: Unique prime factorisation lets the exponent of each prime be compared separately.

solution:
1. Use 18=2·32, 6=2·3, and 12=22·3. The two sides become 22a+b+c+533a+b+2c+5 and 22b+c+33b+c+10.

2. Equality of prime powers gives 2a+b+c+5=2b+c+3 and 3a+b+2c+5=b+c+10. Therefore b=2a+2 and c=5−3a.

3. Hence a+b+c=a+(2a+2)+(5−3a)=7. A positive integer solution does exist: a=1,b=4,c=2. Positivity of c excludes larger positive a. Answer C.
